pr_title: show parametric setters and getters in editor help
pr_body:
Fixes #35090 
All setters and getters were ignored by `editor_help.cpp`. The program now check for parametric setters and getters in the same way as in #30125, and displays them in the editor docs.

issue_context.title: Some methods appear in xml files, but not in the editor
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
3.2 beta6

**Issue description:**
For example the `get_patch_margin()` in `NinePatchRect`. It has an entry in the xml file of the class, but you can't find it in the editor help. This probably applies to all getters/setters that use a default enum argument.
comments:
It does appear, as the getter of the four `patch_margin_*` properties.

But yes, composite setters with 2 arguments or getters with 1 argument are a bit unconventional and are not really documented in the best way - but they're also not really meant to be used, their implementation is a backend detail.

> It does appear, as the getter of the four patch_margin_* properties.

But you can also write the description (unlike other setters/getters) and it's nowhere to be seen. That's the main problem.

Oh I see. That's a bug in the editor indeed.

We chose to expose those in the classref explicitly since their documentation is a bit more than just "sets <property>", as what property is set depends on an enum value. See #30125.

Seems like I did not check that they'd actually appear in the editor, there might be some code to filter them out.

review_comments: I think it would be better to prevent adding those to `skip_methods` in the first place, instead of filtering them out on update.
Do you recommend that because it saves space?

Well, mainly because it would be cleaner from an implementation point of view. If you parse data to create a map of methods that should be skipped, and you already know at this point that some of those actually shouldn't be skipped, they should not be added to the map in the first place.

That being said, I had a quick look and the `skip_methods` is generated while parsing properties and not methods, so doing the check done here might not be trivial, so I guess the solution you used is the good one.
